the GIL prevents parallel bytecode execution
processes or native code give real parallelism

text: How do you write Python that's easy to test?
reference_answer: Push side effects to the edges and keep the core as functions that take values and return values. Inject dependencies rather than importing them deep inside, so a test can substitute one without patching module globals. Heavy mocking is usually a signal the design is wrong, not the test.
expected_points: separate pure logic from side effects
inject dependencies instead of hard-coding them
avoid reliance on global or module-level state
heavy patching indicates a design problem
